# Harbour Line: a long road

The proposal for the Harbour Line was first drawn up in 1998, when the regional council commissioned a study of congestion on the coast road. The study found that traffic on the road had doubled in a decade.

Planning took far longer than expected. Three separate environmental reviews were needed, and the final route was not approved until 2014.

## Construction and cost

Work began in March 2017. The line runs for 41 kilometres and includes the 6.2 km Orlen Tunnel, the longest in the country.

The original budget was 1.8 billion euros. By 2023 the cost had risen to 3.4 billion euros after delays caused by unstable rock in the tunnel section.

## Delays and disputes

The contractor, Brandt Civil, blamed the government for late land purchases, while ministers blamed the contractor for poor management. An independent audit in 2022 found fault on both sides.

The audit recommended that 14 changes be made to future projects, including a single accountable manager.

## What riders can expect

Trains will run every 10 minutes at peak times and every 20 minutes otherwise. The journey from Harbourton to Eastgate will take 34 minutes, down from 71 minutes by road.

A single fare will cost 6.50 euros, with a monthly pass at 120 euros.

## Opening day

The line opens on 9 September 2025. Free travel will be offered for the first week, and the Transport Minister, Lena Voss, will ride the first train.

Engineers warned that the signalling system will be tested for six months after opening and that short closures should be expected.
